text:
alex: Heads up - doing nsys runs against the distroless-produced runtime and we lose all source/line info in the timeline. Kernels show up but stacks are file: <unknown> and line blank. Anyone seen this with distroless images?

sarah: yup saw this once. distroless usually doesn't include /usr/lib/debug or build-id pairs. nsys/CUPTI need debug info available to map addresses -> file/line.

pranav: a few quick checks: (1) was binary built with -g? (2) is there a .gnu_debuglink or build-id that points to a debug file not present in the container? (3) cupTI version matched to driver/runtime?

alex: binary has -g and -fno-omit-frame-pointer, built in CI. readelf -n shows a Build ID, but in container "readelf -n /app/server" returns the ID but there's no /usr/lib/debug/... that matches. CUPTI logs show a warning: "CUPTI: failed to read debug info for address 0x..."

dan: that matches: debug info referenced by build-id is normally in /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/xx/xxxx.debug on Debian/Ubuntu. Distroless base images strip those. nsys will still collect addresses, but symbolization to file/line needs those external debug files.

elena: also double-check libc/ld versions. If the binary references glibc symbols but the container uses a different distro or musl, some in-kernel unwinders may fail to correlate frames to user-space names.

jen: quick repro steps that worked for me: 1) build with -g -fno-omit-frame-pointer 2) in multistage, copy /usr/lib/debug from a debug-enabled image into the final image (only the debug files) 3) run nsys inside the container. After that trace.nsys-rep shows file/line.

alex: can you paste the dockerfile snippet?

jen: sure:
```
FROM debian:bookworm AS debug
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y libc6-dbg && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

FROM gcr.io/distroless/cc
COPY --from=build /app/server /app/server
COPY --from=debug /usr/lib/debug /usr/lib/debug  # only debug symbols, small-ish for CI cache
ENTRYPOINT ["/app/server"]
```

pranav: alternative: ship an unstripped binary to a sidecar or volume only for profiling runs (avoids shipping debug in prod image). mount the debug file path into container when running nsys. Example: `docker run -v /host/debug:/usr/lib/debug ...`

alex: ran that suggestion locally - after copying debug files into image the nsys timeline had exact file/line and perfetto flame lanes started showing correct source locations.

ci-bot: build 2026-03-15T09:12:01 - warning: CUPTI runtime mismatch: installed CUPTI v12, kernel driver expects v11. Some metrics may be disabled.

elena: CUPTI mismatch can also cause partial symbolization issues for CUDA-related frames. If you're profiling GPU kernels, make sure the driver/CUDA/CUPTI stack versions align with the host/inside container.

dan: extra checks: `readelf -n server | grep -i build` and `eu-readelf --debug-dump=info server` (from elfutils) to confirm debug sections are intact. Also `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=trace ./server` is what we use. If you see addresses only, try `nsys profile --sample=cpu` to get CPU frames too.

alex: note for the ticket: cause = distroless final image missing debug-info (build-id->no debug file) + minor CUPTI version mismatch. fix = include debug files during profiling builds or mount debug dir at run time; ensure CUPTI/driver alignment for GPU frames.

jen: will open a tiny RFC for a profiling image variant in our infra repo (distroless + debug files) and include mount instructions for local runs. cc @sarah @pranav to review.

sarah: 👍 also add troubleshooting checklist: readelf build-id, check /usr/lib/debug, check CUPTI version (nvidia-smi && nvcc --version inside container), run a minimal reproduce with sample workload.

pranav: FYI we should avoid shipping debug symbols to prod images. prefer CI task to build profiling image only.

alex: thanks all — repro + temp fix merged into my branch. will post the trace when it's uploaded.

jen: ping when you have the trace.nsys-rep, I'll verify file/line mapping and close the thread. :thumbsup:
